subject.title: fix(sqlite): allow verified shared wal backports

question: Should OpenClaw permanently support a process-wide operator assertion that an older shared system SQLite contains the WAL-reset backport?
rationale: Version inspection cannot recognize arbitrary distribution backports, while a mistaken assertion can expose persistent SQLite data to the corruption bug; maintainers must choose the permanent trust and documentation contract.

options.title: Accept documented shared override
options.body: Keep the strict default and accept the shared-only override after live Red Hat proof and explicit backport-verification documentation.

options.title: Require recognizable safe versions
options.body: Reject the override and require affected distributions to expose an upstream version OpenClaw can identify as fixed.

options.title: Wait for a capability probe
options.body: Pause the fix until a reliable runtime-level method can verify the backported patch directly.

recommendation.title: Accept documented shared override
recommendation.body: Keep the strict default and accept the shared-only override after live Red Hat proof and explicit backport-verification documentation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent SQLite implementation history makes this person the strongest available owner for the runtime safety contract.
